paper_metadata.title: Reduced anticoagulation strategy is associated with a lower incidence of intracerebral hemorrhage in COVID-19 patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the source population across three academic centers. However, the 'low anti-Xa' group was recruited later in the pandemic, introducing potential selection bias due to evolving clinical practices and viral variants, which is a significant limitation in retrospective cohort comparisons.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (ICH) is objectively defined by CT imaging. However, the lack of routine surveillance imaging means that ICH detection was dependent on clinical suspicion, which could lead to under-reporting of asymptomatic or minor cases.

items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined and categorized into major and minor events.

items.evidence_snippet: When ICH or other cranial pathology was clinically suspected, cranial computed tomography (CCT) was immediately performed. No routine surveillance cranial imaging was performed at any center.
items.reasoning: While CT is a gold standard, the lack of routine screening means the measurement is dependent on clinical detection, introducing potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study is highly susceptible to confounding by time. The 'low anti-Xa' group was treated later in the pandemic when other treatments (dexamethasone, tocilizumab) and clinical experience had improved. While the authors adjusted for some factors, the significant differences in baseline characteristics (age, SOFA, inflammatory markers) and the 'era effect' remain major concerns.
